source.title: Convergent Evolution in Neural Representation Space: Emergent Order in Deep Belief Networks
source.authors: Patrick Krauss; Achim Schilling; Andreas K. Maier; T. Kinfe; C. Metzner

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses convergent learning and the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but does not measure whether representations from different models become more alike. Its main measurements concern class separation and feature redundancy within DBNs.
record.gate_note: The GDV results measure separation of labeled classes within a representation, not similarity between models' distances for the same inputs. The paper does report within-layer weight-direction redundancy and low seed-to-seed variation in aggregate metrics; these are related findings but do not measure the behaviors specified by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper analyses class separation (GDV), probe accuracy, reconstruction, dimensionality and within-layer weight and activity redundancy in single unsupervised DBNs. It never measures representational similarity between two models: no cross-seed feature matching, CKA, stitching or cross-architecture comparison. The only cross-model observation is that aggregate layer-wise curves vary little across five seeds. That is a property-level reproducibility statement, not feature or subspace convergence. Convergent learning and the Platonic Representation Hypothesis appear only in the interpretation and discussion sections.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that unsupervised greedy DBN training reproducibly organises representations around latent class structure. Early layers improve class accessibility, while deeper layers compress into redundant, prototype-like feature directions. They link the seed-to-seed reproducibility and within-layer redundancy to convergent learning and the Platonic Representation Hypothesis descriptively. They state their results do not establish uniqueness or architecture independence.
record.recipe_differences: No direct cross-model representation-similarity method is used; the study measures class geometry and within-DBN feature redundancy.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that GDV and probe accuracy can diverge with depth; class accessibility also varies by dataset and probe.

fits_no_version.finding: Within MNIST DBNs (100 units/layer, 5 seeds), deeper layers develop near-duplicate incoming weight directions (nearest-neighbour |cos| 0.51 to 0.94), correlated activity, and a collapse of weight-matrix dimension that tracks the activity effective dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a single greedily trained DBN, deeper layers contain increasingly redundant neuron weight directions and correlated activity patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise aggregate profiles (GDV, abstraction distance, effective dimension, probe accuracy) vary little across five independently initialised DBNs (Fig. 1, Fig. 4A thin curves). This is stated qualitatively; no cross-seed representational similarity is computed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently initialised unsupervised DBNs reproduce the same layer-wise macroscopic representation statistics.

record.code_released: Complete data and analysis programs will be made available upon reasonable request; no URL stated.
record.peer_reviewed: Frontiers in Complex Systems (venue stated in metadata)
record.problems: The study does not compare representations across models or test convergence with model size or capability. Its detailed weight-redundancy analysis is for MNIST DBNs with 100 neurons per hidden layer; the paper also notes that its results do not establish uniqueness or architecture independence.
record.rows_left_out: Class-separation GDV, reconstruction, dimensionality, and probe results were not catalogued as cross-model convergence outcomes: they measure within-representation properties rather than alignment between models.

untested.parts: All: no comparison of independently trained models of different sizes, architectures, objectives or data.
All: no vision-language or paired-modality data.
Whether DBNs from different seeds share features or subspaces. Only scalar summaries (GDV, D_eff, probe accuracy, reconstruction MSE) are compared across seeds.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.
All: the near-duplicate weight directions are found among neurons within one layer of one model, not across models.
All: the GDV-versus-probe divergence concerns class-separation measures, not cross-model similarity metrics.
All: no cross-model alignment level is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification and all rows' versions ['none'] are correct; no row needs fixing. The rows' states are 'observed' only with respect to their own within-model measures. The title's 'convergent evolution' and the 'Platonic attractors' language are interpretive and backed by no cross-model similarity measurement. Controls in Fig. 2(f,g) are single-seed.

versions.untested_parts: Whether representations of independently trained models align as model size or capability increases, particularly across architectures, objectives, data or modalities.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language model alignment are evaluated.
The paper reports similar aggregate layer-wise profiles across seeds but does not compare cross-seed features or shared representational subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment between different models is tested.
The paper measures redundant weight directions among neurons within a DBN, not recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across different models.
The paper compares class-separation and class-accessibility measures, but does not test how choices of similarity metric or inputs affect cross-model convergence.
No comparison tests whether cross-model alignment is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: MNIST DBNs, 100 neurons per hidden layer (five seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean absolute cosine similarity between incoming weight vectors of neuron pairs within each layer.
rows.value: approximately 0.15 in H1, decreases to approximately 0.13 in H2, then rises almost monotonically to 0.35 in H10
rows.note: This is similarity among neurons within a layer of the same model, not alignment across models.

rows.subject: MNIST DBNs, 100 neurons per hidden layer (five seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured each neuron's absolute weight cosine to its most similar other neuron in the same layer, then averaged across neurons.
rows.value: approximately 0.51 in H1 to 0.94 in H10
rows.note: The reported convergence is among neurons within a model; it does not establish recurring features across models.

rows.subject: MNIST DBNs, 100 neurons per hidden layer (five seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured participation-ratio dimension of the weight matrix after normalizing each neuron's weight vector to unit length.
rows.value: approximately 22.9 in H1, briefly increases to 24.5 in H2, then decreases to 5.3 in H10
rows.note: This measures dimensionality within weight matrices, not similarity between different models.

rows.subject: MNIST DBNs, 100 neurons per hidden layer (five seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean absolute Pearson correlation between activity patterns of neuron pairs.
rows.value: approximately 0.15 in H1 to 0.38 in H10
rows.note: This is within-model neuronal activity dependence, not cross-model representational alignment.

rows.subject: MNIST DBNs, 100 neurons per hidden layer (five seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared signed weight cosine with corresponding signed activity correlation across neuron pairs.
rows.measure: Pearson association of signed weight cosine and signed activity correlation
rows.value: approximately 0.64 in H1 to 0.91 in H10
rows.note: The association concerns neurons within a DBN.

rows.subject: MNIST DBNs, 100 neurons per hidden layer (five seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared absolute weight cosine with absolute activity correlation across neuron pairs.
rows.measure: Spearman association of absolute weight similarity and absolute activity correlation
rows.value: approximately 0.19 in H1 to 0.74 in H10
rows.note: The association concerns neurons within a DBN.
